description: xBD is a benchmark dataset of satellite imagery for automated building damage assessment after disasters, released for the xView2 challenge. It pairs very high resolution images taken before and after events such as floods, hurricanes, wildfires, earthquakes, tsunamis and volcanic eruptions, with 850,736 building polygons across 45,362 square kilometres, each labelled on a four-level damage scale, plus boxes for fire, water and smoke. The producer is the U.S. Defense Innovation Unit with Carnegie Mellon University's Software Engineering Institute, working with disaster response agencies. Coverage is global, event-based, for disasters between 2011 and 2019. Image tiles and JSON labels are downloadable free after creating an xView2 account and accepting the Terms of Data Use, under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 licence. Caveats: non-commercial use only; labels come from imagery, not field surveys; events and building types are skewed to North America; the set is static and its damage scale is coarse. Simulation uses: training damage detection used by emergency services for rapid needs assessment, and observed damage states to validate fragility and hazard exposure models. Related records: Copernicus EMS on-demand mapping (data-copernicus-ems-on-demand-mapping) gives operational damage grading, and CrisisNLP (data-crisisnlp-crisis-informatics-datasets) gives social media damage reports.
